partners.diseaseBName: intellectual developmental disorder with polymicrogyria and seizures
partners.mechanism_chain: TCP1 (HGNC:11509) —DISRUPTS→ TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026); SKIC2 (HGNC:10824) —DISRUPTS→ TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026); TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026) —LEADS_TO→ Polymicrogyria (HP:0001275); TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function mutations in TCP1 and SKIC2 disrupt the TCP1 chaperonin complex's ability to properly fold proteins. This impaired protein folding leads to the accumulation of misfolded proteins, cellular stress, and ultimately contributes to the distinct but overlapping phenotypes of intellectual disability, polymicrogyria, and seizures observed in these two rare diseases.

falsification.text: Demonstration that mutations in TCP1 or SKIC2 do not lead to impaired protein folding or cellular dysfunction in relevant model systems, or identification of distinct molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge on the TCP1 chaperonin complex.
falsification.gnomad_variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in TCP1 or SKIC2 in large population databases like gnomAD, which would suggest the proposed causal genes are incorrect or that the variants are extremely rare and likely de novo.

#### 1. intellectual developmental disorder with polymicrogyria and seizures  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.530)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-390471)

**Proposed mechanism:** TCP1 (HGNC:11509) —DISRUPTS→ TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026); SKIC2 (HGNC:10824) —DISRUPTS→ TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026); TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026) —LEADS_TO→ Polymicrogyria (HP:0001275); TCP1 chaperonin-mediated protein folding (GO:0042026) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function mutations in TCP1 and SKIC2 disrupt the TCP1 chaperonin complex's ability to properly fold proteins. This impaired protein folding leads to the accumulation of misfolded proteins, cellular stress, and ultimately contributes to the distinct but overlapping phenotypes of intellectual disability, polymicrogyria, and seizures observed in these two rare diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in TCP1 or SKIC2 do not lead to impaired protein folding or cellular dysfunction in relevant model systems, or identification of distinct molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge on the TCP1 chaperonin complex. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in TCP1 or SKIC2 in large population databases like gnomAD, which would suggest the proposed causal genes are incorrect or that the variants are extremely rare and likely de novo.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the TCP1 chaperonin complex in both diseases could reveal common therapeutic targets for protein misfolding disorders, potentially leading to treatments that improve protein homeostasis and alleviate core symptoms.
